conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions about your situation.

First, do you have any children that you're responsible for?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do. I have two children - Alex who's 18 and Blake who's 17. They both live at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. To help determine your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex and Blake, I need to understand more about their current situations.

Let me start with Alex, who is 18. Is Alex currently in approved education or training?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex is still in education. He's studying for his A-levels at sixth form college.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: That's helpful, thank you. And what about Blake, who is 17 - is Blake also in approved education or training?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Blake is also in education - she's doing her A-levels as well.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you. Now I need to ask about your living situation. Do you currently live in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect. Just a few more questions to complete the assessment.

Are you currently responsible for both Alex and Blake - meaning you live with them and/or pay at least the equivalent of Child Benefit towards their upkeep (such as food, clothes, or pocket money)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, they both live with me at home, so I'm responsible for them.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you. One more important question: have either Alex or Blake started paid work for 24 hours or more per week, or started claiming benefits in their own right (such as Employment and Support Allowance or Universal Credit)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, neither of them work that much or claim any benefits themselves.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. Let me assess the eligibility for Child Benefit for both Alex and Blake.

Based on what you've told me:
- Both children live with you in the UK
- You are responsible for them
- Alex (18) is in approved education (A-levels at sixth form)
- Blake (17) is in approved education (A-levels)
- Neither is working 24+ hours per week
- Neither is claiming benefits in their own right

According to the rules, you normally qualify for Child Benefit for children under 16, but you'll still qualify if your child is under 20 and they stay in approved education or training. A-level studies at sixth form college count as approved education.

Both Alex and Blake meet the eligibility criteria as they are under 20, in approved education, and living with you.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Good news! You are eligible for Child Benefit for both Alex and Blake.**

Since both of your children are under 20 and in approved education (A-levels), you meet the eligibility criteria. Only one person can claim Child Benefit for each child, so as long as no one else is claiming for them, you should be able to receive it.

Please note: If you or your partner have an individual income over £60,000, you may need to pay the High Income Child Benefit tax charge. You can use the Child Benefit tax calculator on GOV.UK to work out if this applies to you.

If you haven't already claimed Child Benefit, you'll need to make a claim. If you have any other questions, feel free to ask!
